items.title: No Surprises Act Dispute System Costs Surpass $22 Billion - ACA International
items.reason: This article directly addresses financial impacts and costs associated with the No Surprises Act's Independent Dispute Resolution system, which is a core component of NSA implementation relevant to revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: According to ACA International, the costs of administering the No Surprises Act's dispute system have exceeded $22 billion. This figure reflects the financial burden associated with the Independent Dispute Resolution (IDR) process, which handles payment disputes between payers and providers when out-of-network surprise bills occur. The substantial cost accumulation has implications for how healthcare organizations manage their revenue-cycle operations, including dispute resolution expenses and resource allocation related to NSA compliance.

items.title: Froedtert Hospital sues CVS Health alleging fraud and $18M in losses - Milwaukee Journal Sentinel
items.reason: This is a provider lawsuit against a major payer (CVS Health) alleging fraud and quantified financial losses, which directly falls within the litigation and enforcement category of the topic definition.
items.summary: Froedtert Hospital has filed a lawsuit against CVS Health alleging fraud and claiming $18 million in losses. The suit represents a provider-initiated legal action against a major payer entity, alleging business misconduct that directly harmed the hospital financially. This type of provider litigation against payers over claims practices, reimbursement disputes, or contractual violations is a core enforcement development that affects hospital revenue-cycle operations and payer relationships. The outcome could influence how CVS Health processes claims for Froedtert and potentially other providers in the network.

items.title: Maryland sues Optum over 'defective' computer system
items.reason: This is a state attorney general lawsuit against a major payer (UnitedHealth Group/Optum) alleging fraud related to a Medicaid program, which directly falls under payer litigation and enforcement actions that affect revenue-cycle operations.
items.summary: Maryland filed a lawsuit against UnitedHealth Group, specifically its Optum subsidiary, alleging fraud in connection with a defective computer system provided to the state's Medicaid program. The suit challenges the adequacy and functionality of systems that Optum supplied for Medicaid administration, claiming the state was defrauded through the provision of faulty technology. This enforcement action against a major payer affects how states and providers interact with UnitedHealth's Medicaid operations and may have implications for claims processing, payment accuracy, and system reliability across UnitedHealth's platforms.

also.title: Maryland Attorney General Sues UnitedHealth, Optum Over Medicaid System Failure - Franklin County Free Press

items.title: Florida AG sues Prime Therapeutics, Express Scripts for alleged price-fixing
items.reason: This is a state attorney general enforcement action against major pharmacy benefit managers (PBMs) for alleged price-fixing, which directly impacts payer operations and falls squarely within payer litigation and regulatory enforcement.
items.summary: Florida Attorney General James Uthmeier filed suit against Express Scripts and Prime Therapeutics, alleging that their partnership illegally fixes prescription drug prices in violation of antitrust law. The lawsuit targets the PBMs' coordinated pricing practices, which affect the costs that health plans and their members pay for medications. This enforcement action is significant for revenue-cycle teams because PBM pricing practices directly influence drug cost management, member cost-sharing calculations, and plan profitability; successful enforcement could force pricing changes that ripple through claims processing and reimbursement workflows.
